name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: India's capacitor-film theme now has three listed producers, not two: Cosmo First (metalliser rated at 900 MT/yr), JPFL Films (Jindal Poly; Rs 250 cr doubling, commissioning not yet confirmed) and SRF (Rs 277 cr Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant commissioned May 2026). Capacitor film is still a small, undisclosed share of each company's revenue, so film-cycle, balance-sheet and governance factors drive the stocks more than this theme does.
key_points: IndexBox (28 Sep 2026) expects global dielectric capacitor-film demand to grow 6-9% a year over 2026-2035, with 7.5% as its base case. It sees automotive power electronics as the fastest-growing segment at 10-14% a year, and BOPP at 60-70% of volume (S1). A separate IndexBox note gives only ~4.8% a year for BOPP dielectric film alone (S2), and Mordor expects plastic film capacitors to grow 4.86% a year from USD 2.58 bn in 2026 to USD 3.27 bn in 2031 (S3).

Demand is moving to thinner films that withstand higher voltages: IndexBox says film makers are developing 2-4 micron substrates for automotive use, especially 800-volt EV platforms (S1). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1).

India relies on imports. Trade-data firm Volza ranks India the world's 3rd-largest importer of capacitor metallised film, with China supplying 7,867 shipments versus 588 from Japan (S17). Cosmo First said at launch that much of India's electrical-grade capacitor film comes from China (S4).

Cosmo First launched metallised capacitor-grade BOPP (2.5-12 micron) in Dec 2023 with ~750 MT/yr capacity (S4). Its website now rates the metalliser at 900 MT/yr and says a second metalliser is being prepared (S5). Capacitor-film revenue is not disclosed.

SRF, not in the brief's original universe, commissioned phase 1 of a capacitor-grade BOPP plant at Indore on 15 May 2026 at ~Rs 277 cr, with a ~Rs 6 cr phase 2 due in Sep 2026 (S11). It separately won ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr polypropylene-film project for capacitors (S13).

JPFL Films (a Jindal Poly Films subsidiary) plans to double capacitor-film capacity for Rs 250 cr, targeting completion by 2025 and citing a TDK testimonial (S6). We found no confirmation that it has been commissioned. Meanwhile, the May 2025 Nashik fire (estimated damage Rs 2,000 cr) (S8), an FY26 net loss of Rs 1,062 cr (S10) and an Aug 2026 SEBI show-cause notice (S9) dominate the Jindal Poly story.

The ECMS scheme is building domestic demand for capacitor inputs: Dhruv Industries was approved for metallised capacitor film in Mar 2026 (S14), and Globe Capacitors was among 31 approvals worth Rs 7,877 cr in Aug 2026 (S16). Most film-capacitor makers that would buy the film, such as Deki, TDK India and Vishay India, are unlisted.

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: SRF has the newest dedicated capacity: its Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant was commissioned in May 2026 (S11). Management said customer approvals had been secured from several leading customers (S12).
Cosmo First has been making the film longest among listed peers (since Dec 2023) and sells an Al-Zn 'series' metallised film for renewable-energy and EV capacitors (S4, S5).
Downstream power-capacitor makers such as Universal Cables, which makes all-polypropylene power capacitors (S21), could source film locally if domestic supply scales.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Polypropylene resin makes up 50-65% of production cost (S1). China's 35-45% share of global capacity (S1) caps pricing power.
Capacitor film is a small, undisclosed share of revenue at all three producers. Commodity BOPP/BOPET cycles and leverage matter more; Cosmo's net debt/EBITDA was 2.3x at Jun 2026 (S19).
Jindal Poly faces a SEBI show-cause notice dated 6 Aug 2026 over transactions and governance, covering the company, its key managers and promoters; the financial impact is not yet known (S9).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Whether SRF's phase 2 is capitalised in Sep 2026 and whether revenue ramps (S11, S12).
Whether JPFL confirms the capacitor-film doubling is complete (S6), and how the SEBI proceedings progress (S9).
Whether Cosmo First commissions its second metalliser (S5) and starts disclosing capacitor-film volumes.
Further ECMS tranches naming metallised-film or film-capacitor projects (S14, S16).

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film (the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates), usually biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP). It is vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it in a clean room with micro-slitting, at 2.5-12 micron thickness, for AC and DC capacitors used in industrial drives, power electronics, EVs and renewable power systems (S4). Packaging BOPP has none of these requirements. SRF describes its KAPLAR capacitor film as made from high-purity electrical-grade resin, with self-healing properties (a local short burns away the thin metal layer instead of destroying the capacitor) and suitability for oil impregnation (S12).

The film is getting thinner. IndexBox says film makers are developing thinner substrates that withstand higher voltages, typically 2-4 micron for automotive use and especially 800-volt EV platforms. It expects BOPP to stay dominant at 60-70% of volume, with metallised film at 40-50% of value (S1).

subsections.title: Market size and growth: estimates differ

blocks.caption: Third-party market forecasts (each is the publisher's own forecast)
rows: USD 2.58 bn (2026) to USD 3.27 bn (2031), 4.86% CAGR; automotive 30.75% share

blocks.text: The two IndexBox notes cover different scopes: all dielectric films at 7.5% versus BOPP dielectric films alone at ~4.8%. The difference implies that non-BOPP and metallised high-end grades grow faster than BOPP base film. We could not open the Future Market Insights figure, so it is not included.

India is the world's 3rd-largest importer of capacitor metallised film, mostly from China, Japan and South Korea. In Volza's shipment count, China accounted for 7,867 shipments versus 588 for Japan (S17). These are shipment counts, not tonnes or value. We found no official DGCI&S tonnage series for the specific HS line. Globally, China holds 35-45% of capacity (S1).

blocks.caption: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) approvals relevant to capacitor film and film capacitors

blocks.text: The first ECMS tranche (Oct 2025) was described as bringing capacitor-grade polypropylene film into Indian production for the first time (S13). The Mar 2026 tranche of 29 projects totalled Rs 71.04 bn (S15). Each capacitor or metallising line approved raises domestic demand for base film, which today comes mostly from imports.

blocks.text: Cosmo First: the capacitor range includes Al-Zn standard, pure Al, slope/RMF, segmented and 'series' metallised PP films; the company says the series grade targets renewable energy and EVs (S5). Group-level Q1 FY27 net debt was Rs 1,166 cr (2.3x EBITDA), and management says incremental capex over the next couple of years will be largely specialty-focused (S19). The company does not disclose capacitor-film revenue.

SRF: KAPLAR is its capacitor-grade BOPP brand (S12). On its Q1 FY27 call (23 Jul 2026), management said customer approvals had been secured from several leading customers and expected early revenue by the end of Q2, with full capacity in Q1/Q2 of next year (S12). Measured against SRF's size, the theme has the least effect on its share price of the three producers.

Jindal Poly Films: JPFL has cited a TDK testimonial and technical support from group company Treofan (S6). However, Jindal Poly's FY26 consolidated revenue fell to Rs 2,899 cr from Rs 5,335 cr, with a net loss of Rs 1,062 cr (S10), after the May 2025 Nashik fire halted about 70% of production (S8).
None of the three companies reports capacitor-film volumes or revenue separately. Any 'share of revenue' figure seen in the market is an estimate, not a disclosure.

items: Polyplex: lists electrical insulation among its BOPET industrial applications, but its product page names no capacitor-grade film (S22). Not confirmed.
UFlex / Flex Films: sells BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised packaging films; we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S24).
Garware Hi-Tech Films: makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation, but at 10-350 micron (S23), thicker than the 2.5-12 micron capacitor band (S4).

Universal Cables: makes all-PP power capacitors (LT/HT) and power-factor panels, a potential domestic film buyer (S21). FY26 revenue was Rs 3,022.67 cr, with 'steep growth' cited in capacitors and allied power-quality solutions (S20).
Syrma SGS: an ECMS beneficiary for passive-component inputs (copper-clad laminates, coils), not a confirmed film buyer (S25).

blocks.text: Market-cap coverage gap: we found no listed mid-cap pure-play and no listed film-capacitor maker publicly tied to a domestic film supplier. The main buyers (Deki, TDK India, Vishay India) are unlisted, so the investable universe is narrow.

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.text: Cosmo First traded at Rs 849 on 28 Sep 2026: 12.9x P/E, about Rs 2,221 cr market cap, a 52-week range of Rs 577-938, and roughly flat over one year despite 16.9% EPS growth (S18). Jindal Poly traded at Rs 675 on 29 Sep 2026, around 0.97x book, with a 52-week range of Rs 360-1,026 (S10). Neither valuation suggests a capacitor-film premium. Each stock is valued on packaging-film earnings, or in Jindal Poly's case on book value.

Broker coverage we found does not treat this as a theme. HSBC's May 2026 note on SRF credits performance films and specialty chemicals for its earnings forecast (S11), and we found no Indian broker note built around capacitor film. Media coverage is mostly trade-press launch stories (S4, S6).

items: Resin cost: polypropylene makes up 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1) and supplies most of India's imports (S17).
Slow customer qualification: SRF took about 2.5 years from board approval (Oct 2023) to commissioning (May 2026) (S11), and JPFL's 2025 target is unconfirmed (S6).
Small share of revenue: commodity packaging-film cycles dominate earnings (S10, S19).

Governance: the SEBI show-cause notice to Jindal Poly, its key managers and promoters cites several sections of the SEBI Act, including the 15HA penalty provision; the financial impact is not yet ascertained (S9).
SRF phase-2 capitalisation (Sep 2026) and first capacitor-film revenue (S11, S12).
Commissioning of Cosmo First's second metalliser (S5).
Confirmation that JPFL's capacitor-film doubling is complete (S6).
Further ECMS tranches for metallised film and film capacitors; approvals have come in several tranches since Oct 2025 (S13, S15, S16).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Any anti-dumping or import-duty action on capacitor film. None was found as of this edition.

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP (2.5-12 micron); launched Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr (S4); metalliser now rated at 900 MT/yr with a second being prepared (S5).
companies.impact: The longest-running listed producer. Capacitor film is not disclosed separately, so earnings still track packaging film and leverage (net debt/EBITDA 2.3x at Jun 2026) (S19). P/E is 12.9x (S18).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film and committed Rs 250 cr to double capacity by 2025, citing a TDK testimonial (S6).
companies.impact: Commissioning is unconfirmed. The Nashik fire (S8), an FY26 net loss of Rs 1,062 cr (S10) and the Aug 2026 SEBI show-cause notice (S9) outweigh the capacitor-film theme.

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned a capacitor-grade BOPP plant (KAPLAR) at Indore on 15 May 2026 at ~Rs 277 cr (S11); holds ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S13).
companies.impact: The largest-cap entrant, with customer approvals secured (S12). Its size means the theme barely moves group earnings, but SRF adds competition for Cosmo and JPFL.

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S21).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer; its capacitors and power-quality business showed 'steep growth' in FY26 (S20). No film-supply tie-up is disclosed.

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker listing electrical insulation among its industrial applications (S22).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: we found no company-confirmed capacitor-grade product (S22).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Flex Films makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised films (S24).
companies.impact: Has metallising know-how, but we found no capacitor-grade product; third-party claims are unconfirmed (S24).

companies.name: Garware Hi-Tech Films Ltd
companies.role: Makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation, at 10-350 micron (S23).
companies.impact: Its thickness range sits above the capacitor band (S4), so the theme does not currently apply to it.

companies.name: Syrma SGS Technology Ltd
companies.role: ECMS beneficiary for passive-component inputs (copper-clad laminates, coils) (S25).
companies.impact: Part of the broader ECMS passive-component push (S16); not a confirmed capacitor-film buyer.

method: First edition, researched on 30 Sep 2026 with web search and page fetches. We checked company websites, exchange-filing summaries (Regulation 30 disclosures via ScanX), ECMS approval coverage, IndexBox and Mordor forecasts, and market-data pages. Several primary PDFs on BSE/NSE, and pages from Business Standard and PIB, returned HTTP 403. Where those were blocked we cited the search-result excerpts and marked them as such. Where the publication date could not be confirmed, the date shown is the access date (2026-09-30). The Future Market Insights estimate, Cosmo First's capacitor-film revenue, and JPFL's capacitor-line commissioning could not be confirmed and are left out. We found no third-party figure for India's import volumes in tonnes. One ScanX summary of Jindal Poly's FY26 results appeared to mislabel its units, so we used Screener's figures. Polyplex, UFlex and Garware are classed as 'other' because none has a company-confirmed capacitor-grade product. SRF was added to the confirmed producers based on its May 2026 commissioning disclosure. No ratings or price targets are given.
